Indian Restaurant In Covent Garden | Dishoom Dishoom Covent Garden Indian Restaurant All welcome food & drink Reservations Visit us FAQs Menus Visit FAQs Book BOMBAY, 1949 A sultry June evening. Lights glow golden. Candles flicker in the warm breeze that arrives gently through the large open windows of the café. I watch, entranced, as Ruby brings the last bars of her song to a wistful close. Cheers erupt from the audience. She stands at the microphone, grins bashfully. Her sari, draped and perfumed, is bottle-green and gold. She bows slightly. Continue reading Welcome to Dishoom Covent Garden Early silver screen talkies brought an intoxicating world of adventure and liberty to Bombay. Thrilling “all talking, singing, dancing” Indian-made dramas cast a glamorous spell over picture houses, and over the city. The thrill and amazement of the Talkies era is captured within ‘New’ Dishoom Covent Garden. Open all day, every day, serving Bombay comfort food for breakfast , lunch , dinner and evening tipples. All are welcome. Food & Drink at Dishoom Covent Garden Begin your day at Dishoom with breakfast , which might be a Bacon Naan Roll, Akuri or The Big Bombay. Then, lunch deliciously on a Paneer Roomali Roll and fancy Salads, or linger with a feast. Refresh your afternoon with a drop of Chai and a small plate or two. Dine early or dine late. Or just join us for a tipple – perhaps an India Gimlet, or the Premier Padmini Negroni? See menus Covent Garden Specials PRAWN PATHIA Most celebratory dish, befitting for auspicious occasions. Succulent prawns are marinated overnight in ginger, garlic and lime juice, lightly charred by the grill then nestled in a fiery-sweet-tangy tomato masala. All is accompanied with an onion salad for freshness and Roomali Roti for mopping. Best when shared. Food Menu DIAMOND THRILLER Swashbuckling mix of Cointreau, cranberry and Finlandia vodka, with chilli and lime shrub. A nostalgic nod to films starring stuntwoman ‘Fearless Nadia’, who captivated 1940s Bombay. Drinks menu Sate the audience, hold their gaze Reservations at Covent Garden Book a table Dishoom is mostly a walk-in café. All are welcome, any time, no reservations needed. However, if you'd like to make a reservation, groups of any size may book during the day. After 6pm, we accept bookings for groups of six or more. Group Bookings It’s 1949, and the thrill of the Talkies era is in full swing. While cine stars chatter self-importantly, the wealthy hobnob with the beautiful, the rakish and the occasional ne’er-do-wells. Stop – admire our walls. The myriad of artefacts, photographs, portraits, collectables. In their stillness they depict the vivacity, life and glamour of 1930s and 40s Bombay. Book anytime before 6pm. After 6pm, bookings are open for groups of 6+. If your desired time isn’t available, simply come along – we keep most of our tables for walk-ins. Yes, our All Day menu is filled with much-loved vegetarian dishes, including Pau Bhaji, Makhmali Paneer, House Black Daal and Gunpowder Potatoes. We also have a dedicated vegan and gluten-free menu available. All diets are happily fed. Is Dishoom Covent Garden halal-friendly? Location & Arrival How long is the queue at Dishoom Covent Garden? At breakfast and lunchtime , walk right in – there will be little or no queue. After 6pm and on weekends, a queue gathers around the café at busier times. You’ll be refreshed with complimentary chai while you wait, and as soon as space allows, can take a seat at the bar with tipples and snacks while your table is readied. Paneer Roomali Roll 12.90 Delicate handkerchief roll crisped and filled with grilled paneer, onion, peppers and green leaves. Mint chutney on the side. A plate of crispy garlic-ginger-soy-chilli-chicken is a modern café staple. (S) Vegetable Samosas 7.90 Crunchy Punjabi-style shortcrust pastry, pea and potato filling warmly spiced with cinnamon. Tamarind chutney for dipping. (Ve, V) Lamb Samosas 8.70 Gujarati filo (not Punjabi shortcrust) stuffed with minced lamb, onions and spices. Okra Fries 7.90 Fine lady's fingers for the fingers. (Ve, V) Chilli Cheese Toast 7.70 A nostalgia for Bombayites. Green chillies, capsicum and garlic in Cheddar melt on white sliced loaf. (V, S) Prawn Koliwada 11.20 Bombay's Koli (fishermen) Wada (district) recipe: a bowl of delicate, crispy morsels – perfect for chutney-dipping. (S) Pau Bhaji 8.70 An old-time favourite with lovely qualities, pre-eminently nicer than any you have sampled before. Buttery-spicy, mashed vegetables and home-made buns on a Chowpatty tray. Puffed rice, peanuts and Bombay Mix tossed with fresh pomegranate, tomato, onion, lime, tamarind, mint. (Ve, V) Grills First comes the marinade, then the open-air grill. Picture Bademiya in Colaba, a Bombay institution since 1942. A balmy night, with newspapers laid out on old car bonnets. You eat. Savour. Spill. Murgh Malai 14.90 Chicken thigh meat is steeped overnight in garlic, ginger, coriander stems and a little cream. Slightly pink when fully cooked. Charred Lamb Chops 19.90 Two chops of generous proportions lie overnight in raw papaya, yoghurt and humble spices. Blackened on the grill and finished with a thrilling Kashmiri chilli sauce. (S) Masala Prawns 18.90 Each one charred slightly at the edges, succulent and simple, nothing to bamboozle. Sheekh Kabab 14.90 Minced lamb is marinated with green chilli, coriander and cumin, then grilled. (S) Makhmali Paneer 14.50 Such simplicity. Pillows of paneer, marinated, charred and spiced gently. Soft, buttery magnificence with warm masala tingles. (V) Ruby Murray Chicken Ruby 18.90 Tender chicken in a rich, silky makhani sauce. A good and proper curry redolent with spice and flavour. Goan Monkfish Curry 19.90 Choicest monkfish simmered in creamy coconut, tamarind, tomatoes and kokum. Strewn with fragrant curry leaves. Most popular for its sublime balance of aromas. Think quality! Mutton Pepper Fry 20.50 Finest mutton marinated in red chilli, ginger and garlic, then cooked with black peppercorns and whole spices. Robust, spicy and tender. (S) Mattar Paneer 17.70 A steadfast, humble and delicious vegetarian curry, beloved of Bombay families. (V) House Black Daal 11.70 A Dishoom signature dish – dark, rich, deeply flavoured. Lamb Biryani 21.50 Fall-apart leg of lamb bedded in a pot with buttery saffron rice, caramelised onions, rich stock and warming spices. Best with raita. Chicken Berry Britannia 18.90 Tempting and flavourful pot of chicken, ginger, garlic, mint, coriander and rice cooked together in the Kacchi style. An homage to Britannia’s Chicken Berry Pulao, with cranberries. Awadhi Jackfruit Biryani 18.20 Sturdy, savoury jackfruit and delicately flavoured rice, potted, sealed and cooked the traditional way. Adorned with barberries and sultanas. (V) Steamed Basmati Rice 5.50 It means “the fragrant one”. (Ve, V) Veg. side dishes First-class greens and other delectables. Chilli Broccoli Salad (Half Portion) 8.70 Toasted pistachios and shredded mint leaves with finest, greenest broccoli, fresh red chillies, pumpkin and sunflower seeds, dates and lime. (Ve, V) Grilled Greens 7.70 Grilled mangetout and Tenderstem broccoli with lively Bengali mustard dressing. Greens for choosing – not refusing! (Ve, V) Chilli Butter-Bhutta 6.50 Corn-on-the-cob, brushed with butter and grilled over charcoal fire. Finished with chilli, salt and lime, Chowpatty style. (V) Kachumber 6.50 A messy to-do of cucumber, onion and tomato. A little lime lifts the whole affair. (V) Warm Aubergine Chutney 3.90 A rare embellishment of sweet and sour and spice. “Very chatpata” (or lip-smacking), says Chef, “not ordinary.” A little goes a long way. (Ve, V) Raita 5.50 Delicate minty yoghurt, cool as a cucumber. (V) Bread All breads are made by hand and baked to order. Plain Naan 5.50 Freshly baked in the tandoor. (V) Garlic Naan 5.60 With minced garlic and coriander sprinkle. (V) Cheese Naan 6.70 Cheddar is melted inside. (V) Masala Paratha 5.90 Wholewheat flaky-buttery bread. Fresh from the tandoor, with chaat masala and dried mint. (V) Roomali Roti 5.50 Soft handkerchief-thin bread, thrown, stretched and griddled to order on an upturned tawa. (Ve, V) Baba’S Sesame Espresso Martini (Up) 12.90 Baba’s espresso meets Finlandia Vodka, with molasses bitters, chai syrup, white sesame tincture and a smattering of black sesame.
